article:
A photo is not a row

Text is small. A film is not. If you commit every screenshot to GitHub you will hate yourself by week three, and the repo will crawl. If you stuff videos into Postgres you have built a museum that bills you for storage and still serves them slowly.

Images and clips live in object storage, or on YouTube and X, or in a host that was built for blobs. The database stores the address. The page stores the address. The file lives elsewhere.

Where they can live

YouTube for the long cut. X for the short cut. The site embeds both. Imagine makes stills; you still have to put the still somewhere public. A bucket — Vercel Blob, S3, Cloudflare Images — when you need a URL you own.

Scratchbox exists because the Desktop is a bad inbox. The same lesson applies to repos.

How I actually do it

Lessons will get a film slot on the right. The film will not be a 400MB file in this repo. It will be a link. Play can iframe a live toy. That is media as a place, not as a commit.

Where noobs get stuck

Dragging a folder of PNGs into git “just for now.” Or encoding nothing and linking to a file:// URL that only works on their laptop. Or building a custom transcoder on day one.

Film this

Export a 30-second clip. Upload it to YouTube unlisted. Embed it in the chapter slot. Then show the repo size not moving. That is the win.

Do this before chapter 11

  • Decide where films will live. Pick one host.
  • Put one still on the internet. Get a URL that works in a private window.
  • Do not commit the still to the lesson repo if it is heavy.

Next: accounts — who is this person, and why you should not invent passwords first.
